t.E160f.agn: In 1974 JECFA evaluated this substance within a group ADI of 0–5 mg/kg body weight together with beta-carotene, beta-apo-8'-carotenal and the methyl ester of beta-apo-8'-carotenoic acid. In the EU it was not included in the authorised list in 2011 because the manufacturer no longer supplied the substance and the re-evaluation was not supported. In 2016 EFSA separately evaluated the same substance as an egg yolk and skin colourant in poultry feed and set an ADI of 0.015 mg/kg body weight for consumers.
t.E160f.body: Beta-apo-8'-carotenoic acid and its esters are normal breakdown products of apo-carotenal in the body. In rats, only a small part of the ester (methyl ester) given at high doses was absorbed, most being excreted in faeces; in infants it has been reported to be cleared quickly from the blood.
t.E160f.eval: Removed from the EU list of authorised additives in November 2011 (Regulation 1129/2011) because it is no longer produced.
t.E160f.found.0: Not authorised as a food additive in the EU since 2011
t.E160f.prod: A carotenoid produced by chemical synthesis.
t.E160f.regx.0: Not included in the EU authorised list by Commission Regulation (EU) No 1129/2011; the manufacturer no longer supplies it and the re-evaluation was not supported.
t.E160f.regx.1: Group ADI 0–5 mg/kg body weight together with beta-carotene and related carotenoids.
t.E160f.regx.2: Evaluated as a poultry feed additive; ADI for consumers 0.015 mg/kg body weight, no genotoxic potential shown.
t.E160f.summary: An orange pigment derived from carotenoids. Not authorised in the EU since 2011.
t.E160f.what: It was a synthetic carotenoid colour that gave food a yellow-orange colour; it is no longer authorised as a food additive in the EU.
